This is the key stat. The average Fortune 500 customer of Anthropic spends less than .1% of their expenses on Anthropic. 

While that number likely will eventually asymptote somewhere (token prices coming down, and other large enterprise spend areas not going away), there’s no reason it can’t be 10-50X higher than this, reaching a “mere” 1-5% of spend. Which would still be a fraction of what most startups are spending.

Thus, you can see how big of a divide there is between the frontier users of AI and the rest of the world still.

Today, only a microscopically small set of companies are actually using agents for large amounts of background tasks and inside of workflows that aren’t human prompted. This Fortune 500 spend is likely dominated by coding tasks and broad employee productivity use-cases.

But the big jump will come as these enterprises start to rewire their underlying processes for agents, which we’re now in the earliest stages of seeing. Agents processing large amounts of data in the enterprises; swarms doing coding, bio research, cyber, and other large fan out tasks; background workflows executing tasks in processes, and so on. All of these use cases generally are 100X bigger consumers of tokens, and much closer to direct ROI on the spend.

This S-1 gives you a sense of both the strength of the frontier lab business model - even amidst massive competition - and how early we are in the build out of AI.

Microsoft's MAI-Image-2.7-Preview takes #2 on AA-Image-Editing v2.1, close behind OpenAI's GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst (max) and a clear step up from MAI-Image-2.6

MAI-Image-2.7-Preview is Microsoft AI's newest image editing model, succeeding MAI-Image-2.6, released in August.

In our testing, MAI-Image-2.7-Preview scores higher than MAI-Image-2.6 on all 7 editing actions we measure, and ranks #1 on 4 of them: Scene & Style Edit, Text or Symbol Edits, Reasoning-Based Edit, and Enhancement & Restoration. This new model improves on MAI-Image-2.6 with the biggest gains in Composition & Framing (+57 Elo), Text or Symbol Edits (+49) and Scene & Style Edit (+48). We see its best use cases to be in Live-Action Film, Consumer and Frontier edits, where it ranks #1.

MAI-Image-2.7-Preview is available today in MAI Playground for image editing only, with text to image stated to be coming soon.

Congratulations to @MicrosoftAI on the release!

Ling 3.1 Flash 1019, an open weights model and successor to Ling 3.1 Flash, scores 44 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3, up from 41

@AntLingAGI has released Ling 3.1 Flash 1019, an update to Ling 3.1 Flash, their reasoning model with 560B total parameters, 25B active parameters, and a 1M token context window. It scores 44 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3, up from 41 from Ling 3.1 Flash. Like Ling 3.1 Flash, Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 is open weights.

Key results:

➤ Ling 3.1 Flash 1019’s agentic capabilities improve over Ling 3.1 Flash. On AA-Briefcase v1.1, Ling 3.1 Flash 1019’s Elo is 1521, up 124 points from 1397 for Ling 3.1 Flash. Its Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1 is 1653, up from 1617 for its predecessor, an increase of 36 points. On AutomationBench-AA, Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 scores 68%, a 6 point increase from Ling 3.1 Flash’s score of 62%

➤ Ling 3.1 Flash 1019’s makes gains in scientific reasoning compared to its predecessor. Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 scores 43% on Humanity’s Last Exam, a 4-point improvement from 39% for Ling 3.1 Flash. It scores 26% on CritPt, an 8-point increase from 18%.

➤ Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 uses more output tokens per task than Ling 3.1 Flash. Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 uses 145k Output Tokens per Intelligence Index Task, more than 40% higher than Ling 3.1 Flash’s per task usage of 103k output tokens

➤ At $1.49 Cost per Task, Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 is more expensive than Ling 3.1 Flash but scores higher on intelligence. This is primarily driven by the higher number of output tokens used. However, Ling 3.1 Flash 1019  is still less expensive than models such as Mistral Large 4 Preview and GLM 5.3

Additional model details:

➤ Size: 560B total parameters, 25B active

➤ Context window: 1M tokens

➤ Pricing: $0.30 per 1M input tokens and $0.90 per 1M output tokens, with cached input at $0.06 per 1M (80% discount)

➤ License: MIT

➤ Availability: Ling-3.1-flash-1019 is available as an open weights model on Hugging Face, and is accessible through InclusionAI’s first party API

Managed Agents is @CartesiaAI's fully managed platform for building and deploying voice agents. It is a cascaded system: Cartesia's own Ink Speech to Text and Sonic Text to Speech models run around an LLM of the developer's choice. We evaluated Cartesia Managed Agents with GPT-5.5 as the LLM and the Skylar and Daniel voices.

Key takeaways:

➤ Speech Agent Arena: Cartesia Managed Agents scores an Elo of 1115 (95% CI 1086-1144, 685 samples), 98 points above Cartesia Line at 1017 (95% CI 985-1049)

➤ Agentic tasks: On tasks that need tool calls, Cartesia Managed Agents scores an Elo of 1112

➤ Task Success Rate: 91.7% of eligible tool-calling conversations end with the correct final task-completing tool call

Congrats to the @CartesiaAI team!

After a breast cancer diagnosis, one of the hardest questions is whether it will come back.

@SimBioSys is helping doctors and patients better understand that risk. Powered by NVIDIA technology, its FDA-cleared TumorSight Risk analyzes an existing breast MRI alongside pathology and clinical information to estimate the risk of cancer returning at five and ten years.

For women with HR-positive, HER2-negative early-stage breast cancer, those insights can be available before surgery, giving them and their doctors more information as they talk through treatment options.

AI can help give patients and their doctors more information when the decisions ahead feel most difficult.

I built 𝚌𝚙𝚞-𝚌𝚑𝚊𝚝, a reproduction of @openai's findings of covert communication using the CPU.

It runs on a generic host with 2+ Firecracker microVMs with no internet access. Works on x86 and even my M5 chip.

I was able to chat via 3 separate mechanisms:
① CPU contention
② Cache eviction timing
③ DRAM bandwidth contention 

… across multiple CPUs, defeating all Firecracker's production recommendations (no SMT, no KSM, tenants pinned to different cores.)

Essentially, if shared hardware is involved, there's a good chance your agents can communicate covertly. And with really decent latency.

The good news: this is decidedly different from a *side-channel attack* where the agents could steal information (Meltdown/Spectre), a category of attack that providers like Vercel Sandbox mitigate. Further, in our real-world environment, these 'whispering' techniques are much harder to pull off and easier for us to monitor and detect (sampling hardware counters + lots of at-scale statistical data.)

Noteworthy: ironically, OpenAI and Anthropic's models refused to do this work. Open weight models got the job done. I'm worried the labs' stance might backfire and get in the way of helping developers build correct and secure systems. e.g: building a secure sandbox requires having this kind of analysis, and without it, we'll have a less secure world.

Unlimited-OCR-2, same 6-page PDF, three machines, mlx-vlm main. 🔥

Unlimited-OCR-2 is Baidu's open document-parsing model (MIT license, 3.3B parameters). It reads a whole multi-page PDF in one request. I ran the same 6 pages of its own technical report on three machines: the DGX Spark (Hugging Face and SGLang) and two Macs (MLX, through mlx-vlm main). Every output is checked against the PDF's own text.

SPEED
One request: 
- M5 Max 189 t/s
- M3 Ultra 164 t/s
- DGX Spark SGLang 135 t/s
- DGX Spark HF 29 t/s

Batched: 
- DGX Spark 659 tok/s total
- M3 Ultra 334 tok/s total

One document: the Mac wins. A server full of documents: the DGX Spark wins, by about 2x.

QUALITY: BASE VS GUNDAM
The model can read a page two ways. Base mode shrinks it into one view. Gundam mode adds six full-size tiles per page.

In base mode every engine I tried misreads page 3 once a request reaches 4 pages: "Document parsing has undergone..." comes out as "is having undergone" or "recessions have undergone". On the M5 Max it can even loop until the token limit. 
Gundam mode reads it right everywhere, with identical text on both Macs, and mlx-vlm main now uses it by default. The Mac port matches Baidu's native output on 99.8% of text tokens.

Thanks to the Baidu ERNIE Team (@Baidu_Inc) for the model: https://t.co/70OHzl0Tye and https://t.co/mFa1JoaHgE to shuuul for the mlx-vlm port and @Prince_Canuma  for fixing and merging it.

you can make almost any program self-improve btw

step 1: prompt your agent "help me plan comprehensive logging such that we can replay what the user experienced, meaningful internal operations, and visible outcomes"

step 2: setup a daily loop with this prompt "analyze my logs from this program in the past 24h thoroughly, identify broken behaviors, user friction, inefficiencies, and propose improvements sorted by estimated impact"

step 3: watch your code get better every day

if your program collect telemetry from users, you can do aggregated analysis which will give you even better results
